units.en: Having left home for a thousand li to seek a small salary, the local chief handles affairs—why worry about incapacity? Moreover, honoring good and advancing the worthy—the matter is not here."
units.literal: Having left home for a thousand li to seek a small salary, the local chief handles affairs—why worry about incapacity? Moreover, honoring good and advancing the worthy—the matter is not here.'

units.zh: 故其年註擬，無退量者。
units.en: Therefore in that year's appointments, none were rejected for insufficient qualifications.
units.literal: Therefore in that year's appointments, none were rejected for insufficient measure.

units.zh: 及渾瑊與吐蕃會盟之日，上御便殿謂宰相曰：「和戎息師，國之大計，今日將士與卿同歡。」
units.en: On the day when Hun Zhen allied with Tibet, the emperor attended the informal hall and told the chief ministers, "Making peace with the barbarians and resting the armies is a great plan of state. Today soldiers and ministers rejoice together with you."
units.literal: On the day when Hun Zhen allied with Tibet, the emperor attended the informal hall and told the chief ministers: 'Making peace with the barbarians and resting the armies is a great plan of state—today soldiers and ministers rejoice together with you.'

units.zh: 馬燧前賀曰：今之一盟，百年內更無蕃寇。」
units.en: Ma Sui stepped forward in congratulation, saying, "With this one alliance, within a hundred years there will be no more Tibetan raids."
units.literal: Ma Sui stepped forward in congratulation, saying: 'With this one alliance, within a hundred years there will be no more Tibetan raids.'

units.zh: 渾曰：「五帝無誥誓之盟，皆在季末。
units.en: Hun said, "The Five Emperors had no alliances of proclamation and oath. All such came at the end of ages.
units.literal: Hun said: 'The Five Emperors had no alliances of proclamation and oath—all such came at the end of ages.

units.zh: 今盛明之代，豈又行於夷狄！
units.en: In this flourishing and enlightened age, how can it again be practiced with barbarians!
units.literal: In this flourishing and enlightened age, how can it again be practiced with barbarians!

units.zh: 人面獸心，難以信結，今日盟約，臣竊憂之。」
units.en: Human faces with beast hearts—they are hard to bind by trust. Your servant privately worries over today's alliance."
units.literal: Human faces with beast hearts—hard to bind by trust; today's alliance, your servant privately worries over it.'

units.zh: 李晟繼言曰：「臣生長邊城，知蕃戎心，今日之事，誠如渾言。」
units.en: Li Sheng continued, saying, "Your servant grew up on the frontier and knows the Tibetan mind. Today's matter is truly as Liu Hun says."
units.literal: Li Sheng continued, saying: 'Your servant grew up on the frontier and knows the Tibetan mind; today's matter is truly as Hun says.'

units.zh: 上變色曰：「柳渾書生，未達邊事；
units.en: The emperor changed color and said, "Liu Hun is a bookish man and does not understand frontier affairs;
units.literal: The emperor changed color and said: 'Liu Hun is a bookish man and does not understand frontier affairs;

units.zh: 大臣智略，果亦有斯言乎！」
units.en: great ministers with wisdom and strategy—can there truly be such words as well!"
units.literal: great ministers with wisdom and strategy—can there truly be such words as well!'

units.zh: 皆頓首俯伏，遽令歸中書。
units.en: All kowtowed and prostrated themselves. He immediately ordered them to return to the Secretariat.
units.literal: All knocked their heads and prostrated themselves; he immediately ordered them to return to the Secretariat.

units.zh: 其夜三更，邠寧節度韓遊瑰飛驛叩苑門，奏盟會不成，將校覆沒，兵臨近鎮，上驚嘆，即遞其表以示渾。
units.en: That night at the third watch, Binning military governor Han Yougui sent a fast courier to knock at the park gate, reporting that the alliance meeting failed, generals and officers were wiped out, and troops pressed the nearby garrison. The emperor exclaimed in alarm and immediately forwarded the memorial to show Liu Hun.
units.literal: That night at the third watch, Binning military governor Han Yougui sent a fast courier to knock at the park gate, reporting that the alliance meeting failed, generals and officers were wiped out, and troops pressed the nearby garrison; the emperor exclaimed in alarm and immediately forwarded the memorial to show Hun.

units.zh: 詰旦，臨軒慰勉渾曰：「卿文儒之士，而萬里知軍戎之情。」
units.en: At dawn the next day, facing the hall he comforted and encouraged Liu Hun, saying, "You are a literary and Confucian gentleman, yet you knew the feelings of the army a thousand li away."
units.literal: At dawn the next day, facing the hall he comforted and encouraged Hun, saying: 'You are a literary and Confucian gentleman, yet you knew the feelings of the army a thousand li away.'

units.zh: 自此驟加禮異。
units.en: From this point the emperor suddenly added special honors.
units.literal: From this he suddenly added special honors.

units.zh: 時張延賞與渾同列，延賞怙權矜己，而嫉渾守正，俾其所厚謂渾曰：「相公舊德，但節言於廟堂，則重位可久。」。
units.en: At that time Zhang Yanshang served in the same rank as Liu Hun. Yanshang relied on power and prided himself on his person, yet envied Hun's uprightness. He had one he favored tell Hun, saying, "The chief minister's old virtue—if you only restrain your words in the court hall, then a high post may last long."
units.literal: At that time Zhang Yanshang served in the same rank as Hun; Yanshang relied on power and prided himself on his person, yet envied Hun's uprightness; he had one he favored tell Hun, saying: 'The chief minister's old virtue—if you only restrain your words in the court hall, then a high post may last long.'

units.zh: 渾曰：「為吾謝張相公，柳渾頭可斷，而舌不可禁也。」
units.en: Hun said, "Give my thanks to Chief Minister Zhang. Liu Hun's head may be cut off, but his tongue cannot be silenced."
units.literal: Hun said: 'Give my thanks to Chief Minister Zhang—Liu Hun's head may be cut off, but his tongue cannot be silenced.'

units.zh: 自是為其所擠，尋除常侍，罷知政事。
units.en: From this he was squeezed out by Yanshang. He was soon appointed regular attendant and relieved of participation in government.
units.literal: From this he was squeezed out by him; soon he was appointed regular attendant and relieved of participation in government.

units.zh: 貞元五年二月，以疾終，年七十五。
units.en: In the second month of the fifth year of Zhenyuan he died of illness at the age of seventy-five.
units.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Zhenyuan he died of illness at age seventy-five.

units.zh: 有文集十卷。
units.en: He left collected writings in ten fascicles.
units.literal: He left a collected writings in ten fascicles.

units.zh: 渾母兄識，，篤意文章，有重名於開元、天寶間，與蕭穎士、元德秀、劉迅相亞。
units.en: Hun's elder maternal brother Shi was devoted to literature and had a great reputation during the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, ranking alongside Xiao Yingshi, Yuan Dexiu, and Liu Xun.
units.literal: Hun's elder maternal brother Shi was devoted to literature and had a great reputation during Kaiyuan and Tianbao, ranking alongside Xiao Yingshi, Yuan Dexiu, and Liu Xun.

units.zh: 其練理創端往往詣極，當時作者，鹹伏其簡拔，而趣尚辨博。
units.en: In refining principles and opening beginnings he often reached the utmost. Writers of the time all submitted to his concise elevation, yet his bent favored disputation and breadth.
units.literal: In refining principles and opening beginnings he often reached the utmost; writers of the time all submitted to his concise elevation, yet his bent favored disputation and breadth.

units.zh: 渾亦善為文，然趨時向功，非沈思之所及。
units.en: Hun also wrote well, yet he bent to the times and sought achievement—not what deep reflection could reach.
units.literal: Hun also wrote well, yet he bent to the times and sought achievement—not what deep reflection could reach.

units.zh: 渾警辯，好諧謔放達，與人交，豁然無隱。
units.en: Hun was alert in debate and fond of jest and free openness. In dealing with people he was expansive and hid nothing.
units.literal: Hun was alert in debate, fond of jest and free openness; in dealing with people he was expansive and hid nothing.

units.zh: 性節儉，不治產業，官至丞相，假宅而居。
units.en: By nature he was frugal and did not manage estates. Though he reached chief minister, he borrowed a residence to live in.
units.literal: By nature he was frugal and did not manage estates; though he reached chief minister, he borrowed a residence to live in.

units.zh: 罷相數日，則命親族尋勝，宴醉方歸，陶陶然忘其黜免。
units.en: Within days of leaving the chief ministry he would order kin to seek scenic spots, feast until drunk before returning, and forget his dismissal in contentment.
units.literal: Within days of leaving the chief ministry he would order kin to seek scenic spots, feast until drunk before returning, and forget his dismissal in contentment.

units.zh: 時李勉、盧翰皆退罷居第，相謂曰：「吾輩方柳宜城，悉為拘俗之人也。」
units.en: At that time Li Mian and Lu Han had both retired and lived at their residences. They said to each other, "Compared with Liu of Yicheng, we are all people bound by convention."
units.literal: At that time Li Mian and Lu Han had both retired and lived at their residences; they said to each other: 'Compared with Liu of Yicheng, we are all people bound by convention.'

units.zh: 史臣曰：張鎰、蕭復、柳渾，節行才能訏謨亮直，皆足相明主，平泰階，而盧杞忌之於前，延賞排之於後，管仲有言：「任君子，使小人間之，害霸也。」
units.en: The historiographer says: Zhang Yi, Xiao Fu, and Liu Hun—in integrity, conduct, talent, and outspoken, bright uprightness—all were sufficient to assist an enlightened ruler and level the grand stairway. Yet Lu Qi envied them before and Yanshang excluded them after. Guan Zhong said, "Employ the gentleman and let petty men come between—this harms hegemony."
units.literal: The historiographer says: Zhang Yi, Xiao Fu, and Liu Hun—in integrity, conduct, talent, and outspoken, bright uprightness—all were sufficient to assist an enlightened ruler and level the grand stairway; yet Lu Qi envied them before and Yanshang excluded them after. Guan Zhong said: 'Employ the gentleman and let petty men come between—this harms hegemony.'

units.zh: 德宗黜賢相，位奸臣，致硃泚、懷光之亂，是失其人也，豈尤其時哉！
units.en: Emperor Dezong dismissed worthy chief ministers and placed treacherous ministers in rank, bringing about the disorders of Zhu Ci and Huai Guang. This was losing the right men. How can one blame the times alone!
units.literal: Emperor Dezong dismissed worthy chief ministers and placed treacherous ministers in rank, bringing about the disorders of Zhu Ci and Huai Guang—this was losing the right men; how can one blame the times alone!

units.zh: 河清歿於王事，乃顯忠貞；
units.en: Heqing died in royal service and thereby displayed loyalty and steadfastness;
units.literal: Heqing died in royal service and thereby displayed loyalty and steadfastness;

units.zh: 從一舉自奸人，固宜循默。
units.en: Liu Congyi was raised by treacherous men and properly ought to have kept silent.
units.literal: Congyi was raised by treacherous men and properly ought to have followed silence.

units.zh: 贊曰：得人則興，失人則亡。
units.en: The encomium says: Gain the right men and flourish; lose them and perish.
units.literal: The encomium says: Gain the right men and flourish; lose them and perish.

units.zh: 鎰、復、渾去，宗社其殃。
units.en: When Yi, Fu, and Hun departed, the altars of state met calamity.
units.literal: When Yi, Fu, and Hun departed, the altars of state met calamity.

units.zh: 李華兄事德秀，而友蕭穎士、劉迅。
units.en: Li Hua honored Dexiu as an elder brother and befriended Xiao Yingshi and Liu Xun.
units.literal: Li Hua treated Dexiu as an elder brother, and was friends with Xiao Yingshi and Liu Xun.

units.zh: 然各有病，元病酒，劉病賞物，蕭病貶惡太亟、獎能太重。
units.en: Yet each had a flaw: Yuan's was wine; Liu's was cherishing possessions; Xiao's was condemning evil too harshly and praising talent too lavishly.
units.literal: Yet each had a flaw: Yuan's flaw was wine; Liu's was cherishing possessions; Xiao's was condemning evil too urgently and praising talent too heavily.

units.zh: 或問所長，華曰：「德秀誌當以道紀天下，迅當以《六經》諧人心，穎士當以中古易今世。
units.en: When asked what each excelled at, Hua said: "Dexiu aimed to order the empire by the Way; Xun aimed to harmonize men's hearts with the Six Classics; Yingshi aimed to replace the present age with the middle antiquity.
units.literal: When asked wherein each excelled, Hua said: "Dexiu's intent was to order the empire by the Way; Xun's was to harmonize men's hearts with the Six Classics; Yingshi's was to replace the present age with the middle antiquity.

units.zh: 德秀欲齊愚智，迅感一物不得其正，穎士呼吸折節而獲重祿，不易一刻之安易，於孔子之門，皆達者歟！
units.en: Dexiu wished to level the foolish and the wise; Xun was stirred whenever a single thing fell short of its proper place; Yingshi would bend and bow with every breath to win heavy rewards, unwilling to trade a moment's ease—yet are all of these adept men within Confucius's gate?
units.literal: Dexiu wished to make the foolish and the wise equal; Xun was moved whenever a single thing failed to attain its proper place; Yingshi would bend and bow for breath to obtain heavy emoluments, unwilling to trade one moment's ease—yet within Confucius's gate, are these all adept men?

units.zh: 穎士若百煉之剛，不可屈，使當廢興去就、一生一死間，而後見其節。
units.en: Let Yingshi be steel tempered a hundred times, impossible to bend; set him at the turning point between a dynasty's rise and fall, between life and death—then you see his integrity.
units.literal: Let Yingshi be steel refined a hundred times, impossible to bend; let him face the going and staying of dynasties, the single span between life and death—then you see his integrity.

units.zh: 穎士尤罪子長不編年而為列傳，後世因之，非典訓也。
units.en: Yingshi especially faulted Master Zichang for not compiling year-by-year annals and writing biographical accounts instead, which later generations followed—this was not canonical teaching.
units.literal: Yingshi especially faulted Master Zi-chang for not compiling annals but writing biographical accounts, which later generations followed—this was not canonical instruction.

units.zh: 自《春秋》三家後，非訓齊生人不錄。
units.en: After the three schools of the Spring and Autumn, he recorded only what could instruct and regulate the living.
units.literal: After the three schools of the Spring and Autumn, only what instructed and regulated the living was recorded.

units.zh: 刑部員外郎劉從一為吏部郎中、兼中丞；
units.en: Liu Congyi, outer vice director of punishments, was appointed director of the personnel ministry and concurrent vice censor-in-chief.
units.literal: Liu Congyi, outer vice director of punishments, was made director of the personnel ministry and concurrent vice censor-in-chief;

units.zh: 李勉，字玄卿，鄭王元懿曾孫也。
units.en: Li Mian, whose courtesy name was Xuanqing, was a great-grandson of Prince Zheng, Yuanyi.
units.literal: Li Mian, styled Xuanqing, was a great-grandson of Prince Zheng Yuanyi.

units.zh: 勉幼勤經史，長而沉雅清峻，宗於虛玄，以近屬陪位，累授開封尉。
units.en: As a boy Mian applied himself diligently to the classics and histories. In maturity he was reserved, refined, and austere, inclined toward Daoist subtlety, and through proximity to the throne was repeatedly appointed marshal of Kaifeng.
units.literal: Mian in youth applied himself to the classics and histories; grown up, he was grave, elegant, clear, and lofty, devoted to the abstruse and mystical, and by virtue of close imperial kinship received successive appointments as marshal of Kaifeng.

units.zh: 德宗嗣位，加檢校吏部尚書，尋加平章事。
units.en: When Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne, Mian was made acting minister of personnel and soon appointed chief councilor.
units.literal: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, Mian was made acting minister of personnel; soon he was made chief councilor.

units.zh: 父擇言，為漢褒相岐四州刺史、安德郡公，所歷皆以嚴干聞。
units.en: His father Zeyan held the posts of prefect over Han, Bao, Xiang, and Qi and bore the title Duke of Ande; wherever he served, he was known for stern efficiency.
units.literal: His father Zeyan served as prefect of the four prefectures Han, Bao, Xiang, and Qi, and as Duke of Ande; in every post he was known for severity and capability.

units.zh: 至德初，從至靈武，拜監察御史。
units.en: In the early Zhide period he accompanied the court to Lingwu and was appointed investigating censor.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide era he followed the emperor to Lingwu and was appointed investigating censor.

units.zh: 大歷二年，來朝，拜京兆尹、兼御史大夫，政尚簡肅。
units.en: In 767 he came to court and was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and censor grandee. His rule was marked by simplicity and austerity.
units.literal: In the second year of the Dali era he came to court and was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and concurrently censor grandee; his administration favored simplicity and severity.

units.zh: 四年，除廣州刺史，兼嶺南節度觀察使。
units.en: In the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Guangzhou and military governor and observation commissioner of Lingnan.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Guangzhou and concurrently military governor and observation commissioner of Lingnan.

units.zh: 十年，拜工部尚書。
units.en: In the tenth year he was appointed minister of works.
units.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed minister of works.

units.zh: 十一年，汴宋留後田神玉卒，詔加勉汴州刺史、汴宋節度使。
units.en: In the eleventh year Tian Shenyu, acting military governor of Bian-Song, died. An edict appointed Mian prefect of Bian and military governor of Bian-Song.
units.literal: In the eleventh year Bian-Song acting military governor Tian Shenyu died; an edict additionally made Mian prefect of Bianzhou and military governor of Bian-Song.

units.zh: 建中元年，檢校左僕射，充河南汴宋滑亳河陽等道都統，餘如故。
units.en: In 780 he was made acting left vice director and supreme commander of the Henan, Bian-Song, Hua-Bo, He-Yang, and related circuits, with his other posts unchanged.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong he was made acting left vice director and appointed supreme commander of Henan, Bian-Song, Hua-Bo, He-Yang, and other circuits; the rest remained as before.

units.zh: 四年，李希烈反，以他盜為名，悉眾來寇汴州。
units.en: In 783 Li Xilie rebelled. Rallying under another rebel's banner, he led his full army against Bianzhou.
units.literal: In the fourth year Li Xilie rebelled; under the name of another bandit he led his entire force to invade Bianzhou.

units.zh: 貞元四年卒，年七十二，上頗愍悼之，冊贈太傅，賻物有差，喪葬官給。
units.en: He died in 788 at the age of seventy-two. The emperor was deeply grieved and posthumously ennobled him as Grand Tutor, granted funeral gifts of appropriate rank, and provided state support for his burial.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged seventy-two; the emperor was much moved and mourned him; by patent he was posthumously made Grand Tutor; funeral gifts were graded; burial expenses were supplied by the state.

units.zh: 克復西京，累歷清要，四遷至河南少尹。
units.en: After the recovery of Chang'an he rose through a series of prestigious posts, reaching vice governor of Henan after four promotions.
units.literal: After recovering the Western Capital, he passed through successive posts of pure and important rank, being promoted four times to vice governor of Henan.

units.zh: 勉不為之屈，竟為所抑，出歷汾州、虢州刺史，改京兆尹、檢校右庶子、兼御史中丞、都畿觀察使。
units.en: Mian refused to bend and was ultimately blocked by Li Fuguo. He was sent out as prefect of Fen and Guo, then appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, acting right vice grand mentor, censor-in-chief, and observation commissioner of the capital region.
units.literal: Mian would not yield to him and in the end was suppressed by him; he went out to serve successively as prefect of Fenzhou and Guozhou, then was changed to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, made acting right vice grand mentor, and concurrently censor-in-chief and observation commissioner of the capital region.

units.zh: 尋兼河南尹，明年罷尹，以中丞歸西台，又除江西觀察使。
units.en: He soon also served as metropolitan governor of Henan. The following year he left that post and returned to the Censorate as chief censor, then was appointed observation commissioner of Jiangxi.
units.literal: Soon he was additionally made metropolitan governor of Henan; the next year he was removed as governor and returned to the western bureau as censor-in-chief, then was appointed observation commissioner of Jiangxi.

units.zh: 忠臣遇下貪虐，明年為麾下所逐，詔復加勉汴宋節度使，移理汴州，餘並如故。
units.en: Zhongchen governed with greed and cruelty and was driven out by his own troops the following year. An edict restored Mian as military governor of Bian-Song and transferred his headquarters to Bianzhou; his other titles remained unchanged.
units.literal: Zhongchen treated his subordinates with greed and cruelty; the next year he was driven out by his own troops; an edict again made Mian military governor of Bian-Song, transferred his administration to Bianzhou, and left the rest as before.

units.zh: 累表辭位，遂罷知政事，加太了太保。
units.en: He repeatedly asked to resign. He was removed from the chief council and appointed Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to resign his post, was removed from participation in government affairs, and was made Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 賊帥陳莊連陷江西州縣，偏將呂太一、武日升相繼背叛，勉與諸道力戰，悉攻平之。
units.en: The rebel leader Chen Zhuang overran prefectures and counties across Jiangxi. Subordinate generals Lü Taiyi and Wu Risheng rebelled in succession. Mian fought alongside troops from other circuits and subdued them all.
units.literal: The bandit chief Chen Zhuang successively seized prefectures and counties of Jiangxi; the subordinate generals Lü Taiyi and Wu Risheng rebelled in turn; Mian fought hard together with the various circuits and attacked and pacified them all.

units.zh: 詔勉與李忠臣、馬燧等攻討，大破之，悅僅以身免。
units.en: An edict ordered Mian, Li Zhongchen, Ma Sui, and others to attack them. The rebels were routed and Tian Yue barely escaped with his life.
units.literal: An edict ordered Mian, together with Li Zhongchen, Ma Sui, and others, to attack and suppress them; they inflicted a great defeat, and Yue barely escaped with his life.

units.zh: 靈曜北走，勉騎將杜如江擒之以獻，代宗褒賞甚厚。
units.en: Li Lingyao fled north, but Mian's cavalry officer Du Rujiang captured him and presented him as a prisoner. Emperor Daizong rewarded Mian handsomely.
units.literal: Lingyao fled north; Mian's cavalry general Du Rujiang seized him and presented him captive; Daizong rewarded him very generously.

units.zh: 勉城守累月，救援莫至，謂其將曰：「希烈兇逆殘酷，若與較力，必多殺無辜，吾不忍也。」
units.en: Mian held the city for months, but no relief came. He told his generals, "Xilie is savage and cruel. If we fight him head on, countless innocents will die. I cannot bring myself to do that."
units.literal: Mian defended the city for months; relief did not arrive; he said to his generals, "Xilie is vicious, rebellious, and cruel; if we match strength with him, many innocents will surely be killed—I cannot bear it."

units.zh: 遂潛師潰圍，南奔宋州。
units.en: He secretly led his troops out through the siege lines and fled south to Songzhou.
units.literal: He then secretly led his troops in breaking the encirclement and fled south to Songzhou.

units.zh: 勉乃哀之，上言曰：「元惡未殄，遭點污者半天下，皆欲澡心歸化。
units.en: Moved to pity, Mian memorialized the throne: "The chief villain is not yet destroyed. Half the empire has been tainted by association, and all wish to purify their hearts and submit. If we execute them all, we will drive the world into the rebels' arms.
units.literal: Mian then pitied him and memorialized, saying, "The chief villain is not yet destroyed; those who were stained number half the empire, and all wish to cleanse their hearts and return to allegiance.

units.zh: 若盡殺之，是驅天下以資兇逆也。」
units.en: To slaughter them all would be to drive the whole world to feed the rebels."
units.literal: If we kill them all, this is driving the empire to supply the vicious and rebellious."

units.zh: 勉詢將吏曰：「上方藉牧宰為人父母，豈以譖言而殺不辜乎！」
units.en: Mian asked his officers and staff, "The throne now depends on local magistrates to be fathers and mothers to the people. How can it put an innocent man to death on a whispered accusation?"
units.literal: Mian questioned his generals and officials, saying, "His Majesty now relies on local administrators as fathers and mothers to the people—how can he kill the innocent on the basis of slander!"

units.zh: 部人有父病，以蠱道為木偶人，署勉名位，瘞於其隴，或以告，曰：「為父禳災，亦可矜也。」
units.en: A subordinate whose father was ill used sorcery to fashion a wooden figure, inscribed it with Mian's name and title, and buried it on his father's grave. When someone reported this, Mian said, "He did it to ward off disaster for his father. That deserves pity."
units.literal: A man of his command, whose father was ill, used sorcery to make a wooden doll, inscribed it with Mian's name and rank, and buried it on his father's mound; someone reported this, and Mian said, "He did it to avert disaster for his father—this may be pitied."

units.zh: 及勉蒞職旬月，朝恩入監，府吏先期有請，勉曰：「軍容使判國子監事，勉候太學，軍容宜厚具主禮。
units.en: About ten days after Mian took office, Yu Chao'en came to the directorate. The prefectural clerks asked in advance how to receive him. Mian said, "As army-observing commissioner supervising the Directorate of Education, he should be received at the Imperial College with full honors befitting the host.
units.literal: When Mian had been in office about ten days and Chao'en entered the directorate, the prefectural clerks made a request in advance; Mian said, "The army-observing commissioner who supervises the Directorate of Education—Mian awaits him at the Imperial College; the commissioner should generously provide the host's rites.

units.zh: 勉忝京尹，軍容倘惠顧府廷，豈敢不具蔬饌。」
units.en: As metropolitan governor I would be unworthy if he did not visit my yamen; but should he deign to come to the prefectural offices, I would of course provide a meal—nothing more."
units.literal: Mian, unworthy as metropolitan governor—if the commissioner should graciously visit the prefectural court, how would I dare not provide vegetables and food."

units.zh: 對曰：「天下皆知其奸邪，獨陛下不知，所以為奸邪也。」
units.en: Mian answered, "The whole world knows he is treacherous and corrupt. Only Your Majesty does not know it. That is precisely what makes him treacherous and corrupt."
units.literal: He replied, "All the world knows he is wicked and treacherous; only Your Majesty does not know—this is why he is wicked and treacherous."

units.zh: 勉坦率素淡，好古尚奇，清廉簡易，為宗臣之表。
units.en: Mian was forthright and unpretentious, loved antiquity and valued the unusual, and lived with incorruptible simplicity. He was a model among the imperial clan.
units.literal: Mian was frank and open, plain by nature, fond of antiquity and devoted to the unusual, incorrupt, simple, and easy in manner—a model among imperial clansmen.

units.zh: 累為河東節度王思禮、朔方河東都統李國貞行軍司馬，尋遷梁州都督、山南西道觀察使。
units.en: He served successively as expeditionary vice marshal under Hedong military governor Wang Sil and under Shuofang-Hedong supreme commander Li Guozhen, then was appointed military governor of Liangzhou and observation commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
units.literal: He repeatedly served as expeditionary vice marshal for Hedong military governor Wang Sil and for Shuofang-Hedong supreme commander Li Guozhen, and soon was transferred to military governor of Liangzhou and observation commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

units.zh: 善鼓琴，好屬詩，妙知音律，能自制琴，又有巧思，
units.en: He played the zither well, enjoyed composing poetry, had a fine ear for music, could build his own instruments, and was gifted with inventive skill.
units.literal: He was skilled at playing the zither, fond of composing poetry, subtle in understanding pitch and mode, able to make zithers himself, and also possessed of ingenious ideas.

units.zh: 及代歸，至石門停舟，悉搜家人所貯南貨犀象諸物，投之江中，耆老以為可繼前朝宋璟、盧奐、李朝隱之徒。
units.en: When he left office and returned north, he moored at Shimen, gathered every piece of southern treasure—ivory, rhinoceros horn, and the like—that his household had accumulated, and threw it all into the river. The elders held that he could stand beside such paragons of integrity as Song Jing, Lu Huan, and Li Chaoyin of the previous reign.
units.literal: When he was replaced and returned, at Shimen he moored his boat, searched out all the southern goods, rhinoceros horn, ivory, and other things his household had stored, and cast them into the river; the elders thought he could follow in the line of Song Jing, Lu Huan, and Li Chaoyin of the former dynasty.

units.zh: 時升平日久，且汴州水陸所湊，邑居龐雜，號為難理，勉與聯尉盧成軌等，並有擒奸擿伏之名。
units.en: Peace had lasted many years, and Bianzhou—where land and water traffic met—was crowded and chaotic, notorious as difficult to administer. Mian, along with associate marshal Lu Chenggui and others, earned a reputation for apprehending wrongdoers and uncovering concealed crimes.
units.literal: The age was long at peace, and moreover Bianzhou, where land and water routes converged, had sprawling, tangled settlements and was called hard to govern; Mian, together with the associate marshal Lu Chenggui and others, all won fame for seizing villains and exposing hidden crimes.

units.zh: 大將管崇嗣於行在朝堂背闕而坐，言笑自若，勉劾之，拘於有司，肅宗特原之，歎曰：「吾有李勉，始知朝廷尊也。」
units.en: The general Guan Congsi sat in the mobile court's audience hall with his back to the throne, chatting and laughing as though unconcerned. Mian impeached him and had him held by the proper authorities. Emperor Suzong personally pardoned Guan and sighed, "Only with Li Mian do I learn that the court commands respect."
units.literal: The great general Guan Congsi at the mobile court sat in the audience hall with his back to the imperial presence, talking and laughing as if at ease; Mian impeached him and had him detained by the appropriate office; Suzong specially pardoned him and sighed, saying, "With Li Mian, I now know that the court is honored."

units.zh: 時關東獻俘百餘，詔並處斬，囚有仰天歎者，勉過問之，對曰：「某被脅制守官，非逆者。」
units.en: More than a hundred captives from east of the Pass were presented at court, and an edict ordered them all put to death. One prisoner looked up to heaven and sighed. Mian stopped to question him, and the man answered, "I was forced to hold office under duress; I was no rebel."
units.literal: At the time more than a hundred captives from east of the Pass were presented; an edict ordered them all executed. Among the prisoners one sighed toward heaven; Mian passed by and questioned him, and he replied, "I was coerced into holding office and was not a rebel."

units.zh: 勉以故吏前密縣尉王晬勤干，俾攝南鄭令，俄有詔處死，勉問其故，乃為權幸所誣。
units.en: Mian had appointed his former subordinate Wang Hui, once magistrate of Mi County, to act as magistrate of Nanzheng on account of his diligence and ability. Soon an edict ordered Wang's execution. When Mian inquired, he learned that Wang had been framed by powerful favorites at court.
units.literal: Mian, because his former subordinate Wang Hui, former magistrate of Mi County, was diligent and capable, had him act as magistrate of Nanzheng; shortly an edict ordered his execution; Mian inquired the reason and found he had been slandered by the powerful and favored.

units.zh: 即停詔拘晬，飛表上聞，晬遂獲宥，而勉竟為執政所非，追入為大理少卿。
units.en: He at once withheld the edict, detained Wang Hui, and sent an urgent memorial to the throne. Wang was spared, but Mian was censured by the chief ministers and recalled to the capital as vice minister of justice.
units.literal: He immediately halted the edict, detained Hui, and sent an urgent memorial to inform the throne; Hui thus obtained pardon, but Mian in the end was faulted by those in power and was recalled to serve as vice minister of justice.

units.zh: 王晬後以推擇拜大理評事、龍門令，終有能名，時稱知人。
units.en: Wang Hui was later recommended and appointed reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Longmen. He retained a reputation for competence to the end, and contemporaries praised Mian for discerning talent.
units.literal: Wang Hui later, through recommendation, was appointed reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Longmen; to the end he had a reputation for ability, and men of the time praised Mian for knowing men.

units.zh: 肅宗將大用勉，會李輔國寵任，意欲勉降禮於己。
units.en: Suzong was on the point of giving Mian major responsibility when Li Fuguo, then in high favor, expected Mian to show him deference.
units.literal: Suzong was about to employ Mian on a grand scale when Li Fuguo, enjoying favor and trust, wished Mian to lower ritual deference toward himself.

units.zh: 朝恩聞而銜之，因不復至太學，勉亦尋受代。
units.en: Yu Chao'en took offense and never visited the college again. Mian was soon replaced in his post.
units.literal: Chao'en, hearing this, bore a grudge; he therefore did not again go to the Imperial College, and Mian soon afterward was replaced.

units.zh: 勉至，遣將李觀與容州刺史王翃人並力招討，悉斬之，五嶺平。
units.en: On arriving, Mian sent the general Li Guan and Rongzhou prefect Wang Hong to campaign together against them. All were executed and the Five Ridges were pacified.
units.literal: When Mian arrived, he sent the general Li Guan and Rongzhou prefect Wang Hong to join forces in recruiting and suppressing them; all were beheaded and the Five Ridges were pacified.

units.zh: 前後西域舶泛海至者歲才四五，勉性廉潔，舶來都不檢閱，故末年至者四十餘。
units.en: In earlier years only four or five Western merchant ships reached port each year. Mian was incorruptible by nature and never inspected incoming vessels, so that in his last year more than forty ships arrived.
units.literal: Before and after, Western Region ships that crossed the sea to arrive numbered only four or five a year; Mian by nature was incorrupt, and when ships came he did not inspect them at all; therefore in his final year more than forty arrived.

units.zh: 及滑亳永平軍節度令狐彰卒，遺表舉勉自代，因除之。
units.en: When Linghu Zhang, military governor of the Huai-Bo-Yongping circuit, died, his final memorial recommended Mian as his successor, and Mian was appointed in his place.
units.literal: When Huai-Bo Yongping Circuit military governor Linghu Zhang died, his final memorial recommended Mian to replace him, and he was accordingly appointed.

units.zh: 未行，汴州將李靈曜阻兵，北結田承嗣，承嗣使侄悅將銳兵戍之。
units.en: Before Mian could take up the post, the Bianzhou general Li Lingyao rebelled and allied himself with Tian Chengsi to the north. Chengsi sent his nephew Tian Yue with elite troops to hold the city.
units.literal: Before he set out, the Bianzhou general Li Lingyao obstructed with arms, joined in the north with Tian Chengsi, and Chengsi sent his nephew Yue to lead crack troops to garrison the place.

units.zh: 既而李忠臣代鎮汴州，而勉仍舊鎮。
units.en: Li Zhongchen was then assigned to garrison Bianzhou while Mian remained at his original command.
units.literal: Shortly afterward Li Zhongchen replaced him in garrisoning Bianzhou, while Mian remained at his former command.

units.zh: 既至朝廷，素服請罪，優詔復其位，勉引過備位而已。
units.en: On reaching court he appeared in plain dress to accept blame. A gracious edict restored his rank, and Mian simply acknowledged his fault and resumed his seat.
units.literal: When he reached court he wore plain robes to request punishment; a gracious edict restored his position; Mian merely acknowledged fault and filled his seat.

units.zh: 他日，上謂勉曰：「眾人皆言盧杞奸邪，朕何不知！
units.en: On another occasion the emperor said to Mian, "Everyone says Lu Qi is treacherous and corrupt. Do you think I do not know it?
units.literal: Another day the emperor said to Mian, "Everyone says Lu Qi is wicked and treacherous—how would I not know!

units.zh: 或曰：「勉失守梁城，亦可貶也。」
units.en: Some said, "Mian lost Bianzhou and ought to have been demoted."
units.literal: Some said, "Mian lost and abandoned Liang City—he too could be demoted."

units.zh: 況勉應變非長，援軍莫至，又其時關輔已俶擾矣，人心已動搖矣。
units.en: Moreover Mian was not a master of crisis, no relief force came, the capital region was already in turmoil, and popular morale was collapsing.
units.literal: Moreover Mian was not long skilled in meeting change; relief armies did not arrive; moreover at that time the capital region was already in uproar and men's hearts were already shaken.

units.zh: 歷處、隨、唐、睦四州刺史，由黔中觀察為鄂、岳、沔、蘄、安、黃團練觀察使，時元和十一年也。
units.en: He served as prefect of Chu, Sui, Tang, and Mu prefectures, then rose from observation commissioner of Qianzhong to training and observation commissioner over E, Yue, Mian, Qi, An, and Huang—in 816.
units.literal: He served as prefect of four prefectures—Chu, Sui, Tang, and Mu; from Qianzhong observation commissioner he became training and observation commissioner of E, Yue, Mian, Qi, An, and Huang; this was in the eleventh year of Yuanhe.

units.zh: 會於頔、杜黃裳家私事發，連逮鑒虛下獄。
units.en: When private scandals at the homes of Yu Di and Du Huangshang came to light, Jianxu was implicated and imprisoned.
units.literal: When private affairs at the homes of Yu Di and Du Huangshang came to light, Jianxu was implicated and imprisoned.

units.zh: 李希烈揣知之，上表數崇義過惡，請率先誅討。
units.en: Li Xilie divined their intent and submitted a memorial listing Chongyi's crimes, asking to take the lead in punishing him.
units.literal: Li Xilie guessed their intent and submitted a memorial listing Chongyi's faults, asking to take the lead in punishment.

units.zh: 無幾，希烈既平崇義，果有不順之跡，上思承言，故驟加擢用。
units.en: Before long Xilie had pacified Chongyi and indeed showed signs of rebellion; the emperor recalled Cheng's warning and swiftly promoted him.
units.literal: Before long Xilie had pacified Chongyi and indeed showed signs of disobedience; the emperor recalled Cheng's words and swiftly promoted him.

units.zh: 建中二年七月，拜同州刺史、河中尹、晉絳都防禦觀察使。
units.en: In the seventh month of 781 he was made prefect of Tong, mayor of the Hezhong metropolitan area, and commissioner of defense and observation for Jin and Jiang.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Jianzhong he was made Prefect of Tong, Mayor of the Hezhong metropolitan area, and Commissioner of Defense and Observation for Jin and Jiang.

units.zh: 希烈既破崇義，擁兵襄州，遂有其地。
units.en: After Xilie defeated Chongyi he massed troops at Xiangzhou and thereupon held that territory.
units.literal: After Xilie had defeated Chongyi he massed troops at Xiangzhou and thereupon held that territory.

units.zh: 希烈不能屈，遂剽虜闔境所有而去，襄、漢為之空。
units.en: Xilie could not break him; he then plundered everything of value in the circuit and withdrew, leaving Xiang and Han stripped bare.
units.literal: Xilie could not break him; he then plundered all goods in the circuit and departed, and Xiang and Han were left empty.

units.zh: 上悅之，每對朝臣多稱希烈忠誠。
units.en: The emperor was pleased; before the court he often praised Xilie's loyalty.
units.literal: The emperor was pleased; facing court ministers he often praised Xilie's loyalty.

units.zh: 承自黜陟回，因奏之曰：「希烈將兵討伐，必有微勛，但恐立功之後，縱恣跋扈，不稟朝憲，必勞王師問罪。」
units.en: When Cheng returned from his commission, he memorialized: "Xilie will surely win some merit on campaign—but I fear that once he has merit he will grow insolent and defiant, disregard imperial authority, and the royal army will be forced to march against him."
units.literal: When Cheng returned from his commission, he memorialized: "Xilie will surely win some merit campaigning—but I fear that after merit he will grow insolent and defiant, disobey imperial law, and the royal army will labor to punish him."

units.zh: 朝廷慮不受命，欲以禁兵送承，承請單騎徑行。
units.en: The court feared Xilie would refuse the appointment and wished to send palace troops to escort Cheng; Cheng asked to ride through alone.
units.literal: The court feared he would not accept orders and wished to send palace troops to escort Cheng; Cheng asked to ride alone straight through.

units.zh: 既至，希烈處承於外館，迫脅萬態，承恬然自安，誓死王事。
units.en: When he arrived, Xilie lodged Cheng in an outer guesthouse and assailed him with every sort of coercion; Cheng remained calm, sworn to the throne unto death.
units.literal: When he arrived, Xilie lodged Cheng in an outer guesthouse and coerced him with every manner of threat; Cheng remained calm and at ease, sworn to royal service unto death.

units.zh: 初，希烈雖歸蔡州，留將校等於襄州守當時所掠得財帛什物等，後使襄、漢，往來不絕。
units.en: At first, though Xilie had returned to Cai prefecture, he left officers at Xiang to guard the goods plundered there; afterward traffic between Xiang and Han never ceased.
units.literal: At first, though Xilie had returned to Cai prefecture, he left officers and clerks at Xiang to guard the property and goods looted at the time; afterward envoys between Xiang and Han never ceased.

units.zh: 承亦使腹心臧叔雅往來許、蔡，厚結希烈腹心周曾、王玢、姚憺等。
units.en: Cheng also sent his trusted agent Zang Shuya back and forth between Xu and Cai, lavishly cultivating Xilie's intimates Zhou Ceng, Wang Bin, Yao Tan, and others.
units.literal: Cheng also sent his trusted follower Zang Shuya back and forth between Xu and Cai, richly cultivating Xilie's intimates Zhou Ceng, Wang Bin, Yao Tan, and others.

units.zh: 及曾等謀殺希烈，以眾歸朝，多承首建謀也。
units.en: When Ceng and the others plotted to kill Xilie and bring their forces back to the court, the plan owed much to Cheng's original design.
units.literal: When Ceng and the rest plotted to kill Xilie and bring the hosts back to the court, the plan owed much to Cheng's first design.

units.zh: 三年八月，代王縉為東都留守，充河南、淮西、山南東道副元帥，平章事如故。
units.en: In the eighth month of the third year, he replaced Wang Jin as guardian of the eastern capital, deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East, while retaining his grand councilorship.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, he replaced Wang Jin as guardian of the eastern capital, served as deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East circuits, and remained grand councilor as before.

units.zh: 迅被卿佐服，居賓友，謀治亂根源，參乎元精，乃見其妙。
units.en: Let Xun wear the robes of a chief minister's aide, dwell among guests and friends, and deliberate the roots of order and chaos while communing with the primordial essence—then you see his subtlety.
units.literal: Let Xun wear the garb of a chief minister's aide and dwell among guests and friends, deliberating the roots of order and chaos and communing with the primordial essence—then you see his subtlety.

units.zh: 迅世史官，述《禮》、《易》、《書》、《春秋》、《詩》為《古五說》，條貫源流，備古今之變。
units.en: Xun, a historian of his age, set forth the Ritual, Changes, Documents, Annals, and Odes in "The Ancient Five Expositions," threading origins and developments and encompassing change from antiquity to the present.
units.literal: Xun, being a historian of the age, set forth the Ritual, Changes, Documents, Annals, and Odes in "The Ancient Five Expositions," threading origins and developments and encompassing change ancient and modern.

units.zh: 及路嗣恭代少遊，到州，即日杖殺，識者以是減魏之名，多路之政。
units.en: When Lu Sigong replaced Shaoyou and reached the prefecture, he had Mingguan flogged to death that same day. The knowing held that this diminished Wei's reputation and enhanced Lu's.
units.literal: When Lu Sigong replaced Shaoyou and reached the prefecture, he had Mingguan beaten to death that same day. The knowing judged that this diminished Wei's name and enhanced Lu's governance.

units.zh: 大歷六年三月己未卒於官，贈太師。
units.en: On the third day jiwei of the third month of 771 he died in office and was posthumously created grand preceptor.
units.literal: On the third day jiwei of the third month of the sixth year of Dali he died in office; posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 十二年，河南尹齊抗復論其弊，以為：「軍興，國用稍廣，隨要而稅，吏擾人勞。
units.en: In year twelve, Henan prefect Qi Kang renewed the critique: "War had widened spending, ad hoc taxes multiplied, and clerks tormented the people.
units.literal: In the twelfth year, the Prefect of Henan Qi Kang again discussed its abuses, holding: "When war arose, state use grew somewhat broad; taxes followed need and clerks harassed the people with labor.

units.zh: 陛下變為兩稅，督納有時，貪暴無容其姦。
units.en: Your Majesty's two-tax reform timed collection and checked official extortion.
units.literal: Your Majesty changed to the two taxes, with supervised payment on schedule, so greed and violence had no room for fraud.

units.zh: 二十年間，府庫充牣。
units.en: Within twenty years the treasuries filled.
units.literal: Within twenty years the treasuries were full.

units.zh: 但定稅之初，錢輕貨重，故陛下以錢為稅。
units.en: At first cash was cheap and goods dear, so the throne taxed in money.
units.literal: But when tax was first fixed, cash was light and goods heavy, so Your Majesty took cash as the tax.

units.zh: 今錢重貨輕，若更為稅名，以就其輕，其利有六：吏絕其姦，一也；
units.en: Now money is dear and goods cheap. Renaming the tax to follow commodity values would yield six gains: first, officials could not cheat;
units.literal: Now cash is heavy and goods light; if the tax name were changed to follow the light value, the benefits would be six: clerks would lose their fraud, first;

units.zh: 人用不擾，二也；
units.en: second, the people would not be harassed;
units.literal: the people's use would not be disturbed, second;

units.zh: 靜而獲利，三也；
units.en: third, revenue would rise without turmoil;
units.literal: profit gained in stillness, third;

units.zh: 用不乏錢，四也；
units.en: fourth, the treasury would not lack coin;
units.literal: use would not lack cash, fourth;

units.zh: 不勞而易知，五也；
units.en: fifth, rules would be simple;
units.literal: without labor yet easy to know, fifth;

units.zh: 農桑自勸，六也。
units.en: sixth, farming and sericulture would revive themselves.
units.literal: farming and sericulture would encourage themselves, sixth.

units.zh: 百姓本出布帛，而稅反配錢，至輸時復取布帛，更為三估計折，州縣升降成姦。
units.en: Farmers produce cloth and silk, yet taxes are assessed in cash and collected in cloth after triple valuation—prefectures manipulate prices at will.
units.literal: The common people fundamentally produce cloth and silk, yet tax is assigned in cash; at delivery time cloth and silk are again taken, further subjected to triple valuation and folding, and prefectures and counties raise or lower to commit fraud.

units.zh: 若直定布帛，無估可折。
units.en: Fix payment in cloth and silk and valuation fraud ends.
units.literal: If cloth and silk were fixed directly, there would be no valuation to fold.

units.zh: 蓋以錢為稅，則人力竭而有司不之覺。
units.en: Cash taxation exhausts labor while officials remain blind to it.
units.literal: Generally, taking cash as tax, human power is exhausted yet the offices do not perceive it.

units.zh: 今兩稅出於農人，農人所有，唯布帛而已。
units.en: The two taxes fall on farmers, who own only cloth and silk.
units.literal: Now the two taxes come from farmers; what farmers possess is only cloth and silk.

units.zh: 用布帛處多，用錢處少，又有鼓鑄以助國計，何必取於農人哉？」
units.en: Cloth and silk circulate widely; coin is needed less, and minting aids the treasury—why burden farmers?"
units.literal: Where cloth and silk are used is many, where cash is used few; moreover casting assists state accounts—why must it be taken from farmers?"

units.zh: 至涇州，欲投田希鑒，希鑒偽致禮誘之，與泚俱斬首來獻。
units.en: When they reached Jing Prefecture they wished to surrender to Tian Xijian; Xijian feigned courtesy to lure them in, then beheaded both together with Ci and presented their heads.
units.literal: When they reached Jing Prefecture they wished to surrender to Tian Xijian; Xijian feigned courtesy to lure them in, then beheaded both together with Ci and presented their heads.

units.zh: 建中四年，李希烈叛，寇陷汝州，詔哥舒曜率師攻之，營於襄城。
units.en: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, Li Xilie rebelled and captured Ru Prefecture; the court ordered Geshu Yao to lead troops against him and encamp at Xiangcheng.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, Li Xilie rebelled, raided and captured Ru Prefecture; an edict ordered Geshu Yao to lead troops to attack him and encamp at Xiangcheng.

units.zh: 十月，與朔方節度使司徒郭子儀、河東節度使太尉李光弼等九節度同圍安慶緒於相州。
units.en: In the tenth month he joined Shuofang governor Guo Ziyi, Hedong governor Li Guangbi, and eight other commanders in besieging An Qingxu at Xiangzhou.
units.literal: In the tenth month, together with the Shuofang military governor and Minister of Works Guo Ziyi, the Hedong military governor and Grand Marshal Li Guangbi, and eight other frontier commands, he jointly besieged An Qingxu at Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 五日，至新鄭縣，聞郭子儀已整眾屯谷水，李光弼還太原，炅憂懼，仰藥而卒。
units.en: On the fifth he reached Xinzheng and learned that Guo Ziyi had regrouped at Gushui while Li Guangbi had gone back to Taiyuan. In fear and despair Jiong took poison and died.
units.literal: On the fifth day, reaching Xinzheng County, he heard that Guo Ziyi had already reassembled his force at Gushui and Li Guangbi had returned to Taiyuan; Jiong, anxious and afraid, took poison and died.

units.zh: 於事多遺忘，言元稹不應進士，以父元魯山名進故也，多如此類。
units.en: He often forgot things; he claimed Yuan Zhen should never have taken the jinshi because he had advanced by his father Yuan Lushan's name—errors of that sort were common with him.
units.literal: In affairs he often forgot things; he said Yuan Zhen should not have taken the jinshi examination because his father Yuan Lushan had entered through the name Jin—many errors of this kind.

units.zh: 李靈曜之亂也，河南節帥所據，多不奉法令，征賦亦隨之；
units.en: During Li Lingyao's rebellion the Henan military governors mostly ignored imperial law, and tax collection suffered likewise;
units.literal: During the rebellion of Li Lingyao, the military governors holding Henan mostly did not obey laws and edicts, and tax collection followed suit;

units.zh: 敕御史大夫李涵、右散騎常侍蕭昕、兵部侍郎袁傪、禮部侍郎常袞、諫議大夫杜亞同推，載皆款伏。
units.en: The emperor ordered Chief Censor Li Han, Regular Attendant Xiao Xin, Vice Minister of War Yuan Kan, Vice Minister of Rites Chang Gun, and Remonstrance Officer Du Ya to join the inquiry; Zai confessed to all charges.
units.literal: An edict ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Han, Right Regular Attendant Xiao Xin, Vice Minister of War Yuan Kan, Vice Minister of Rites Chang Gun, and Remonstrance Officer Du Ya to join the inquiry; Zai confessed to all charges.

units.zh: 時宰臣常袞專政，以晏久掌銓衡，時議平允，兼司儲蓄，職舉功深，慮公望日崇，上心有屬。
units.en: Chancellor Chang Gun then dominated the court. Yan had long controlled appointments with a reputation for fairness and also managed state granaries with deep achievement; Gun feared Yan's rising prestige and that the emperor might favor him for higher office.
units.literal: At that time Chancellor Chang Gun monopolized government; because Yan had long controlled personnel selection, public opinion deemed him fair, and he also managed storage—his duties were fulfilled and his achievements deep; Gun feared Yan's public standing rising daily and that the sovereign's heart might turn to him.

units.zh: 竊忌之，乃奏晏朝廷舊德，宜為百吏師長，外示崇重，內實去其權。
units.en: Secretly jealous, he memorialized that Yan, a veteran of the court, should be mentor to all officials—honoring him in name while stripping his real authority.
units.literal: Secretly jealous, he memorialized that Yan was an old merit of the court and should be moral teacher to all officials—outwardly showing honor while inwardly stripping his power.

units.zh: 及奏上，以晏使務方理，代其任者難其人，使務、知三銓並如故。
units.en: When the memorial was submitted, because Yan's fiscal duties were still in order and no replacement could be found, his transport commission and control of the three selection boards remained unchanged.
units.literal: When the memorial was submitted, because Yan's commission affairs were still being managed and no replacement could be found, his commission duties and charge of the three selection boards remained as before.
